inline_comments.comment: The tooltip element is created and assigned to `tooltipElem` AFTER the mouseover/mouseout event handlers have already been registered against it. While this works today because JS closures capture the variable by reference (not by value), it is architecturally inverted and fragile — any future code between handler registration and this assignment that could synchronously trigger a mouse event would reference the old (pre-reassignment) value. The tooltip creation should be moved to before the event handler setup, consistent with how `classDb.ts` structures this.

`// @ts-ignore TODO: fix this` suppresses a type error with no explanation of what the error is or why it is being ignored. Prefer `// @ts-expect-error <reason>` (which will fail if the error disappears, acting as a self-cleaning suppression) and include a brief description of the type mismatch so future maintainers can address it.

Changing the selector from `svg.selectAll('g.node')` to `svg.selectAll('g').filter(...)` is significantly broader. SVG diagrams routinely nest `<g>` elements — a parent `<g>` with a `title` attribute and a descendant `<g>` that also has a `title` would both receive mouseover handlers. On hover, both could fire, causing the tooltip to update twice and potentially flicker or show the wrong content. The original `g.node` was deliberately scoped to class diagram nodes. If the intent is to support tooltips on more element types, the selector should be explicit (e.g., `g.node, g.label`) rather than a catch-all.

The pattern `this.escapeHtml(title).replace(/<br\/>/g, '
')` — escape everything, then selectively un-escape `
` — is correct but non-obvious. A brief comment explaining the intent (e.g., `// Escape all HTML except
which is used for line breaks in diagram titles`) would help future maintainers understand why this is safe and intentional, and avoid accidentally 'simplifying' it in a way that reintroduces XSS.

general_comments.comment: `classDb.ts` gained an `escapeHtml` method to sanitize title content before passing it to `.html()`, preventing XSS via user-authored diagram titles. The equivalent mouseover handler in `flowDb.ts` does not appear to receive the same treatment in this diff — if `flowDb.ts` still uses unescaped `.html()` or a less safe pattern for its tooltip content, this creates an inconsistent security posture between diagram types. The same HTML-escaping protection should be applied uniformly.

The tooltip appearance is now defined by 11 identical `.style()` calls duplicated verbatim between `classDb.ts` and `flowDb.ts`. This violates DRY and will cause the two implementations to drift over time (e.g., someone updates the font size in one file but not the other). A shared utility function such as `createTooltipElement(): Selection<HTMLDivElement, unknown, HTMLElement, unknown>` in a common module would eliminate the duplication and keep both diagram types visually consistent. Additionally, the agent found that some diagram types (e.g., `flowchart/styles.ts`) already define `.mermaidTooltip` styles in CSS — duplicating the same properties as inline styles creates two competing style sources for the same element, which can cause confusion and specificity conflicts.
